nina-ops: FYI - multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on /v1/embed after last deploy (12:05 UTC). p95 ~ 400ms -> 850ms, p99 -> 2.6s. attaching traces and a sanitized log snippet: https://s3.redwood/esc/trace-acct_abc123 (redacted)

sam-oncall: @nina-ops on it. Any region/model pattern?

nina-ops: Mostly us-west1, model redwood/llama-13b-q4. Traffic concentrated from acct_abc123 (ACME). Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/embed \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input":"<~20k chars>"}'
```
Latency shoots when payloads are large. p99 correlates with long-seq requests and KV cache miss rate.

mohit-sre: Jumping in. Quick triage: sounds like tail amplification + cold KV cache + recent kernel change in runtime. Short-term mitigations we can apply now: enable circuit breaker, cap concurrency for that model, and route traffic for acct_abc123 to a smaller quantized fallback in another region. Proposed guardrail values (temporary): p99_threshold_ms=1500, max_concurrency=200, edge_rate_limit=300rps.

jess-support: @mohit-sre please paste exact steps so I can update ACME.

mohit-sre: Steps I'm going to run (will paste commands):
1) Patch account routing to set fallback model and circuit breaker:
```
curl -X PATCH 'https://controlplane.internal/v1/routes/acct_abc123' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"route": {"primary": "redwood/llama-13b-q4", "fallback": "redwood/llama-7b-quant"}, "policy": {"circuit_breaker": {"p99_ms": 1500, "max_concurrent": 200, "window_s": 60}}}'
```
2) Apply edge rate-limit override for acct_abc123 -> 300rps:
```
kubectl exec -n edge edge-config -- ./bin/edgectl apply-rate-limit --account acct_abc123 --rps 300
```
3) Kick a warmup job to prefill KV cache for hot prefixes:
```
./scripts/prefetch_prefixes.sh --account acct_abc123 --model redwood/llama-13b-q4 --window 3600
```
I can run (1) and (2) now and monitor p95/p99 for 15m.

sam-oncall: Good. If spikes don't drop, rollback the deploy (sha=abcdef123) and escalate to infra-eng. Also create a temporary alert: latency.p99 /v1/embed acct_abc123 > 2s for 5m -> page.

nina-ops: executing (1) and (2) now. pinging ACME support with heads-up. :phone: 

alert-bot: [ALERT] latency.p99 /v1/embed acct_abc123 breached 2.6s at 12:07 UTC -> paging on-call.

mohit-sre: Confirmed: routing patched, circuit-breaker active, edge limit applied. Initial telemetry: tail latency decreased ~40% within 3m. p99 down from 2.6s -> 1.4s. No increase in 5xxs so far.

jess-support: Messaging sent to customer: "We've routed your traffic to a fallback model and applied short-term rate limits and circuit breakers while we investigate. We'll follow up with timeline/next steps."

sam-oncall: Ops TODO captured: - bake circuit-breaker config into model deployment template - add pre-deploy perf regression gate (fail deploy if p99 increases > 20%) - add canary traffic runner for long-seq workloads

nina-ops: Scheduling 2pm PT postmortem sync. I'll move notes to incidents channel and attach traces.

mohit-sre: Longer-term recommendations (notes for postmortem): quantize target model variants, improve KV cache heatmap + proactive warming during deploys, and add per-account dynamic throttles for large-request customers. If needed, we can also failover acct_abc123 to eu-west1 fallback (higher latency but more stable) as a secondary fallback.

jess-support: Thanks all. I'll close the support ticket with these actions and keep the customer updated until things are stable. :thumbsup: 

sam-oncall: Closing loop for ops: observed stabilization over 20m window -> p99 ~1.2s, p95 ~420ms. Keep monitoring for 2h before fully relaxing guardrails. If any regression, escalate and rollback.

(END THREAD)
